verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. It verifies n=1 by an explicit positive-integer solution. For n=2, reduction modulo 3 forces 3 to divide a, c, and then b, yielding a strictly smaller positive-integer solution and contradicting minimality. For every fixed n>=3, parity forces b, then a, then c to be even; division by the resulting common powers of 2 again yields a strictly smaller solution for the same exponent, contradicting minimality. These cases exhaust all positive integers n. The statement is self-contained, no prohibited proof patterns occur, and no external references or fact_id citations require checking.
